page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-focused instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon processors operating at 2.5 GHz. Configured with 8 physical cores and 16 virtual CPUs via hyperthreading, the server incorporates 33 MB of Level 3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX and AVX-512F vector extensions. The instance is allocated 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps, while dedicated hardware accelerators and local storage are absent, requiring external network block storage for persistence.

Benchmark evaluations show mid-range throughput across standard enterprise compute tasks. The platform scored 1435.0 points in Geekbench single-core and 8756.0 in multi-core testing, with a PassMark CPU score of 19335.86. Memory subsystem performance records 99.23 GB/sec uncached sequential reads and 57.5 GB/sec writes. In application benchmarks, the server delivers 15.61 million Redis SET operations per second and 16.35 GB/sec in static web serving. For lightweight language models with 135M parameters, prompt processing reaches 1253.79 tokens per second; however, larger 7B model prompt ingestion drops to 31.77 tokens per second, reflecting the constraints of its memory capacity and absence of matrix acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.u1-c1m1.4xlarge provides an economical compute footprint for tasks demanding dedicated processor cycles without large memory allocations. The restrictive 16 GB memory ceiling limits its viability for in-memory databases, large containers, or dense virtualization. However, the balance of 16 dedicated threads and 5 Gbps network bandwidth suits distributed batch processing, parallel compilation, CI/CD pipeline workers, CPU-based compression jobs, and front-end web serving fleets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.4xlarge is an x86_64 instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical Intel Xeon cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of memory and a 5 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network storage volumes. Benchmark metrics place the server in the middle tier of comparable instances, reaching a PassMark CPU score of 19335.86, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8756.0, and 15.61 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 99.23 GB/sec for large uncached reads. The 1:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio represents a trade-off that favors thread concurrency over memory-heavy caching. This profile provides cost-effective throughput for CPU-bound tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web application serving, and multi-threaded data compression workloads that operate within a 16 GB footprint.
